chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who is traveling, then arrives and enters the houses of Kufa: does he complete the prayer or is he a shortener until he enters to his family? He said, 'Rather, he is a shortener until he enters to his family.'

key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Kufa (a major city in Shia jurisprudence)

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler's prayer shortening end upon returning to their city?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific boundary for ending the traveler’s prayer status, ruling that entry into the city proper is insufficient to terminate the *qasr* state. The Imam specifies that the transition to resident (*muqim*) status only occurs upon entering one’s own household, a detail that highlights the practical application of *safar* (travel) in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the importance of physical presence within the domestic sphere as the definitive marker for resuming full four-rak'ah prayers.
